17: /// A type for handling replacements while amortizing allocation.
18: pub struct Replacer<M: Matcher> {
19:     space: Option<Space<M>>,
20: }

22: struct Space<M: Matcher> {
23:     /// The place to store capture locations.
24:     caps: M::Captures,
25:     /// The place to write a replacement to.
26:     dst: Vec<u8>,

32:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
33:         let (dst, matches) = self.replacement().unwrap_or((&[], &[]));
34:         f.debug_struct("Replacer")

41: impl<M: Matcher> Replacer<M> {
42:     /// Create a new replacer for use with a particular matcher.
43:     ///
44:     /// This constructor does not allocate. Instead, space for dealing with
45:     /// replacements is allocated lazily only when needed.
46:     pub fn new() -> Replacer<M> {
47:         Replacer { space: None }
48:     }
49: 
50:     /// Executes a replacement on the given subject string by replacing all
51:     /// matches with the given replacement. To access the result of the
52:     /// replacement, use the `replacement` method.
53:     ///
54:     /// This can fail if the underlying matcher reports an error.
55:     pub fn replace_all<'a>(
56:         &'a mut self,
57:         searcher: &Searcher,
58:         matcher: &M,
59:         mut subject: &[u8],
60:         range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
61:         replacement: &[u8],
62:     ) -> io::Result<()> {
63:         // See the giant comment in 'find_iter_at_in_context' below for why we
64:         // do this dance.
65:         let mut is_multi_line = searcher.multi_line();
66:         if is_multi_line {
67:             if let Some(line_term) = matcher.line_terminator() {
68:                 if line_term == searcher.line_terminator() {
69:                     is_multi_line = false;
70:                 }
71:             }
72:             if let Some(non_matching) = matcher.non_matching_bytes() {
73:                 if non_matching.contains(searcher.line_terminator().as_byte())
74:                 {
75:                     is_multi_line = false;
76:                 }
77:             }
78:         }
79:         if is_multi_line {
80:             if subject[range.end..].len() >= MAX_LOOK_AHEAD {
81:                 subject = &subject[..range.end + MAX_LOOK_AHEAD];
82:             }
83:         } else {
84:             // When searching a single line, we should remove the line
85:             // terminator. Otherwise, it's possible for the regex (via
86:             // look-around) to observe the line terminator and not match
87:             // because of it.
88:             let mut line = Match::new(0, range.end);
89:             let lineterm = searcher.line_terminator();
90:             if lineterm.is_suffix(&subject[line]) {
91:                 let mut end = line.end() - 1;
92:                 if lineterm.is_crlf() {
93:                     if end > 0 && subject.get(end - 1) == Some(&b'\r') {
94:                         end -= 1;
95:                     }
96:                 }
97:                 line = line.with_end(end);
98:             }
99:             subject = &subject[..line.end()];
100:         }
101: 
102:         let &mut Space { ref mut dst, ref mut caps, ref mut matches } =
103:             self.allocate(matcher)?;
104:         dst.clear();
105:         matches.clear();
106: 
107:         let mut last_copy = range.start;
108:         let mut search_at = range.start;
109:         let mut last_match_end: Option<usize> = None;
110:         loop {
111:             if search_at > subject.len() {
112:                 break;
113:             }
114:             let found = matcher
115:                 .captures_at(subject, search_at, caps)
116:                 .map_err(|err| {
117:                     io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Other, err.to_string())
118:                 })?;
119:             if !found {
120:                 break;
121:             }
122:             let m = caps.get(0).unwrap();
123:             if m.start() == m.end() {
124:                 search_at = m.end() + 1;
125:                 if Some(m.end()) == last_match_end {
126:                     continue;
127:                 }
128:             } else {
129:                 search_at = m.end();
130:             }
131:             last_match_end = Some(m.end());
132:             let unmatched_start = last_copy;
133:             let unmatched_end = m.start();
134:             dst.extend(&subject[unmatched_start..unmatched_end]);
135:             last_copy = m.end();
136:             let repl_start = dst.len();
137:             caps.interpolate(
138:                 |name| matcher.capture_index(name),
139:                 subject,
140:                 replacement,
141:                 dst,
142:             );
143:             let repl_end = dst.len();
144:             matches.push(Match::new(repl_start, repl_end));
145:         }
146:         let remaining_start = last_copy;
147:         let remaining_end = subject.len();
148:         dst.extend(&subject[remaining_start..remaining_end]);
149:         Ok(())
150:     }
151: 
152:     /// Return the result of the prior replacement and the match offsets for
153:     /// all replacement occurrences within the returned replacement buffer.
154:     ///
155:     /// If no replacement has occurred then `None` is returned.
156:     pub fn replacement<'a>(&'a self) -> Option<(&'a [u8], &'a [Match])> {
157:         match self.space {
158:             None => None,
159:             Some(ref space) => {
160:                 if space.matches.is_empty() {
161:                     None
162:                 } else {
163:                     Some((&space.dst, &space.matches))
164:                 }
165:             }
166:         }
167:     }

169:     /// Clear space used for performing a replacement.
170:     ///
171:     /// Subsequent calls to `replacement` after calling `clear` (but before
172:     /// executing another replacement) will always return `None`.
173:     pub fn clear(&mut self) {
174:         if let Some(ref mut space) = self.space {
175:             space.dst.clear();
176:             space.matches.clear();
177:         }
178:     }

180:     /// Allocate space for replacements when used with the given matcher and
181:     /// return a mutable reference to that space.
182:     ///
183:     /// This can fail if allocating space for capture locations from the given
184:     /// matcher fails.
185:     fn allocate(&mut self, matcher: &M) -> io::Result<&mut Space<M>> {
186:         if self.space.is_none() {
187:             let caps =
188:                 matcher.new_captures().map_err(io::Error::error_message)?;
189:             self.space =
190:                 Some(Space { caps: caps, dst: vec![], matches: vec![] });
191:         }
192:         Ok(self.space.as_mut().unwrap())
193:     }
194: }

196: /// A simple layer of abstraction over either a match or a contextual line
197: /// reported by the searcher.
198: ///
199: /// In particular, this provides an API that unions the `SinkMatch` and
200: /// `SinkContext` types while also exposing a list of all individual match
201: /// locations.
202: ///
203: /// While this serves as a convenient mechanism to abstract over `SinkMatch`
204: /// and `SinkContext`, this also provides a way to abstract over replacements.
205: /// Namely, after a replacement, a `Sunk` value can be constructed using the
206: /// results of the replacement instead of the bytes reported directly by the
207: /// searcher.
208: #[derive(Debug)]
209: pub struct Sunk<'a> {
210:     bytes: &'a [u8],
211:     absolute_byte_offset: u64,
212:     line_number: Option<u64>,
213:     context_kind: Option<&'a SinkContextKind>,
214:     matches: &'a [Match],
215:     original_matches: &'a [Match],
216: }
217: 
218: impl<'a> Sunk<'a> {
219:     #[inline]
220:     pub fn empty() -> Sunk<'static> {
221:         Sunk {
222:             bytes: &[],
223:             absolute_byte_offset: 0,
224:             line_number: None,
225:             context_kind: None,
226:             matches: &[],
227:             original_matches: &[],
228:         }
229:     }
230: 
231:     #[inline]
232:     pub fn from_sink_match(
233:         sunk: &'a SinkMatch<'a>,
234:         original_matches: &'a [Match],
235:         replacement: Option<(&'a [u8], &'a [Match])>,
236:     ) -> Sunk<'a> {
237:         let (bytes, matches) =
238:             replacement.unwrap_or_else(|| (sunk.bytes(), original_matches));
239:         Sunk {
240:             bytes: bytes,
241:             absolute_byte_offset: sunk.absolute_byte_offset(),
242:             line_number: sunk.line_number(),
243:             context_kind: None,
244:             matches: matches,
245:             original_matches: original_matches,
246:         }
247:     }
248: 
249:     #[inline]
250:     pub fn from_sink_context(
251:         sunk: &'a SinkContext<'a>,
252:         original_matches: &'a [Match],
253:         replacement: Option<(&'a [u8], &'a [Match])>,
254:     ) -> Sunk<'a> {
255:         let (bytes, matches) =
256:             replacement.unwrap_or_else(|| (sunk.bytes(), original_matches));
257:         Sunk {
258:             bytes: bytes,
259:             absolute_byte_offset: sunk.absolute_byte_offset(),
260:             line_number: sunk.line_number(),
261:             context_kind: Some(sunk.kind()),
262:             matches: matches,
263:             original_matches: original_matches,
264:         }
265:     }
266: 
267:     #[inline]
268:     pub fn context_kind(&self) -> Option<&'a SinkContextKind> {
269:         self.context_kind
270:     }

273:     pub fn bytes(&self) -> &'a [u8] {

276:

278:     pub fn matches(&self) -> &'a [Match] {

688:     fn record_matches(
689:         &mut self,

691:         bytes: &[u8],
692:         range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
693:     ) -> io::Result<()> {

695:         if !self.needs_match_granularity {

698:         // If printing requires knowing the location of each individual match,
699:         // then compute and stored those right now for use later. While this
700:         // adds an extra copy for storing the matches, we do amortize the
701:         // allocation for it and this greatly simplifies the printing logic to
702:         // the extent that it's easy to ensure that we never do more than
703:         // one search to find the matches (well, for replacements, we do one
704:         // additional search to perform the actual replacement).
705:         let matches = &mut self.standard.matches;
706:         find_iter_at_in_context(
707:             searcher,
708:             &self.matcher,
709:             bytes,
710:             range.clone(),
711:             |m| {
712:                 let (s, e) = (m.start() - range.start, m.end() - range.start);

715:             },
716:         )?;

718:         if !matches.is_empty()

430: pub fn find_iter_at_in_context<M, F>(
431:     searcher: &Searcher,
432:     matcher: M,
433:     mut bytes: &[u8],
434:     range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
435:     mut matched: F,
436: ) -> io::Result<()>
437: where
438:     M: Matcher,
439:     F: FnMut(Match) -> bool,
440: {
441:     // This strange dance is to account for the possibility of look-ahead in
442:     // the regex. The problem here is that mat.bytes() doesn't include the
443:     // lines beyond the match boundaries in mulit-line mode, which means that
444:     // when we try to rediscover the full set of matches here, the regex may no
445:     // longer match if it required some look-ahead beyond the matching lines.
446:     //
447:     // PCRE2 (and the grep-matcher interfaces) has no way of specifying an end
448:     // bound of the search. So we kludge it and let the regex engine search the
449:     // rest of the buffer... But to avoid things getting too crazy, we cap the
450:     // buffer.
451:     //
452:     // If it weren't for multi-line mode, then none of this would be needed.
453:     // Alternatively, if we refactored the grep interfaces to pass along the
454:     // full set of matches (if available) from the searcher, then that might
455:     // also help here. But that winds up paying an upfront unavoidable cost for
456:     // the case where matches don't need to be counted. So then you'd have to
457:     // introduce a way to pass along matches conditionally, only when needed.
458:     // Yikes.
459:     //
460:     // Maybe the bigger picture thing here is that the searcher should be
461:     // responsible for finding matches when necessary, and the printer
462:     // shouldn't be involved in this business in the first place. Sigh. Live
463:     // and learn. Abstraction boundaries are hard.
464:     let is_multi_line = searcher.multi_line_with_matcher(&matcher);
465:     if is_multi_line {
466:         if bytes[range.end..].len() >= MAX_LOOK_AHEAD {
467:             bytes = &bytes[..range.end + MAX_LOOK_AHEAD];
468:         }
469:     } else {
470:         // When searching a single line, we should remove the line terminator.
471:         // Otherwise, it's possible for the regex (via look-around) to observe
472:         // the line terminator and not match because of it.
473:         let mut m = Match::new(0, range.end);
474:         trim_line_terminator(searcher, bytes, &mut m);
475:         bytes = &bytes[..m.end()];
476:     }
477:     matcher
478:         .find_iter_at(bytes, range.start, |m| {
479:             if m.start() >= range.end {
480:                 return false;
481:             }
482:             matched(m)
483:         })
484:         .map_err(io::Error::error_message)
485: }

487: /// Given a buf and some bounds, if there is a line terminator at the end of
488: /// the given bounds in buf, then the bounds are trimmed to remove the line
489: /// terminator.
490: pub fn trim_line_terminator(
491:     searcher: &Searcher,
492:     buf: &[u8],
493:     line: &mut Match,
494: ) {
495:     let lineterm = searcher.line_terminator();
496:     if lineterm.is_suffix(&buf[*line]) {
497:         let mut end = line.end() - 1;
498:         if lineterm.is_crlf() && end > 0 && buf.get(end - 1) == Some(&b'\r') {
499:             end -= 1;
500:         }
501:         *line = line.with_end(end);
502:     }
503: }
